what_happened: On a straight multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy took over at 4.7s and planned a path that veered right toward the next lane (toward actor 4), even though the recorded route went straight. The ego slowed and steered right across the lane line, and its front hit actor 3, which was driving beside it in the right lane, at 6.4s.

The command was RIGHT and the route turned right, but after handoff the policy steered left across several lanes, away from the route. It ended up about 13 m off the recorded path and left the drivable area at 8.8 s, at about 5.4 m/s. The input flags an at-fault collision, but every collision metric in the frames reads 0, so the confirmed failure is offroad; the camera smearing came only after the ego had already moved far from the recorded path.

On a multi-lane road that bends gently left, the policy kept going straight and drifted right onto the shoulder and dirt verge at about 6 m/s. The recorded route (green) followed the lane leftward, and by 7.3 s the ego was 3.5 m off it and off the road. The camera view was clean before the drift and nothing in the way forced the move.

On a multi-lane highway, the human driver moved left (and the route command switched to LEFT). The ego instead braked hard, from 20 to 8 m/s, and steered right into the next lane, where the semi truck (actor 5) was driving alongside. It hit the truck's side with its front at 8.1 s.

In slow, dense highway traffic, the ego drifted right of the recorded path, about 2.8 m off it at the end, even though the route command was LEFT. It angled toward the silver van (actor 13) ahead and to its right, and its front corner hit the van while slowing from about 4 m/s to 1.8 m/s.

At about 5 m/s on a straight multi-lane highway, the ego left its lane behind car 5 and turned left across the leftmost lane line and the concrete median barrier, ending up off the road. The route went straight ahead and the command was RIGHT. The camera view looked fine before the turn and only smeared once the ego was off the road. The rear contact came after the ego had already left its lane.

After handoff the ego ignored the RIGHT command and steered left across several lanes toward the left road edge, ending 11 m off the recorded path. It side-swiped actor 32, which was travelling in the lane the ego cut into (lateral collision at 7.8 s).

On a multi-lane highway, the policy steered right toward the lane next to it while the route said LEFT and the recorded path stayed in the lane. At 7.0 s the ego's front hit vehicle 3, which was slightly ahead in that right-hand lane.

After the 4.7s handoff the ego was in the rightmost lane of a multi-lane road with a STRAIGHT and then LEFT command. Its planned path (orange) kept bending right instead of following the lane or the human path (green), and the ego drove over the right edge onto the dirt shoulder at about 6.5 m/s, ending 3.6 m off the recorded trajectory. The camera view at 5.3s was clean and the shoulder was clearly visible, so rendering does not explain the steering choice.

The highway bends gently left, but the policy kept heading straight and to the right at about 6 m/s, while the recorded route followed the bend. The ego drifted out of the rightmost lane onto the shoulder and gravel at the road edge, ending up about 3.6 m off the recorded path. The camera view was clean at 5.3 s, when the planned path was already pointing toward the shoulder, so the image doesn't explain the mistake.

On a straight multi-lane freeway with the route command STRAIGHT, the policy took over at 4.7 s and planned a lane change to the right, cutting in between vehicle 4 ahead and vehicle 3 alongside in the right lane. At 6.4 s, about 1.7 m off the recorded path, the ego's front hit vehicle 3, which was already occupying that lane.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy's planned path swung right toward the next lane, behind actor 4. The ego steered right across the lane line and its front struck actor 3, which was driving alongside in that lane, at 6.4s. Steering across the lane line also put the ego offroad. The lead vehicle in the ego's own lane was still about 12 m ahead.

In slow, dense highway traffic with a LEFT command, the ego drifted right of the recorded path (2.8 m off by the end) into the lane behind the slow silver van (actor 13). It closed on the van, braking only gently (4.1 to 1.9 m/s while the gap shrank from 8 m to about 4 m), and hit the van's rear with its front at 8.1 s. The ego was also rear-ended at some point, but the frontal collision with the van came first.

Although the route command was LEFT, the ego left its recorded lane and moved right into the next lane, ending up close behind the silver van (actor 13), about 3 m off the human path. It slowed from 4.1 to 1.8 m/s but not enough, and its front hit the van at 8.1 s.

On a multi-lane freeway, the policy steered right out of the recorded lane even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then LEFT. It moved about 1.9 m off the human path into the lane on its right, and its front hit actor 3, which was travelling alongside and slightly ahead in that lane.

On a multi-lane highway at about 6 m/s, the ego drifted right toward the next lane, even though the route command was LEFT and the recorded human path stayed in the lane. Its front-right corner hit actor 3, which was travelling alongside and slightly ahead in the right lane. The ego was 1.7 m off the recorded path at impact, and the camera showed that car close on the right before contact.

On the highway, logged truck 5 in the lane to the right merged left into the ego's lane. The human driver had moved left and kept speed, but the ego braked hard (21 to 8 m/s), stayed in its lane and ignored the LEFT command, so the truck's side came across its front at 8.0 s. A follower also hit the ego's rear because of the hard braking.

The route command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego braked and steered left, away from the recorded path. It cut diagonally across several lanes toward the left road edge and median, about 10.5 m off the recording, and its front hit vehicle 32 in one of the lanes it was crossing.

The route command was RIGHT and the route line ran to the right, but after handoff the ego braked from about 17.6 to 7.4 m/s and steered left across several lanes toward the left edge of the road. Ending about 10.8 m from the recorded path, it cut across the lane of vehicle 32 and hit it with its side (lateral at-fault collision), with the offroad flag also raised.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego braked from 20 to 8 m/s. Its path then curved right toward the adjacent lane, even though the command was LEFT and the recorded path stayed left. It cut into the side of semi truck 5 in the right lane, making front contact at 8.1s, 4.8 m off the recorded path.

On a multi-lane highway, the route command was STRAIGHT and then LEFT, and the recorded human path moved left. The ego braked from 20 to 8 m/s and steered right instead, cutting into the lane of truck 5 as the truck passed alongside, and hit it with its front at 8.1 s.

The policy took over at 4.6 s in the rightmost lane at about 18 m/s, with no lead vehicle and the command STRAIGHT. The road bends gently left, but the policy's plan held straight and slightly right instead of following the route. By 5.5 s the ego had drifted over the right lane edge toward the curb and was flagged offroad, only 0.7 m from the recorded human path.

After taking over at 4.7s, the ego slowed from about 19 to 11 m/s but steered left, away from the recorded path, which bears right to follow the RIGHT command. At 7.1s it drove off the left edge of the road into the landscaped median, about 7.3 m from the recorded path, with no other actors involved and the camera view clear beforehand.

The road bends left, but the ego kept going roughly straight and crossed the right edge line onto the dirt shoulder by the fence while the route line curved left. It slowed from about 23 to 16 m/s but never steered through the bend; there were no actors nearby and the camera view looked fine before the failure.

The command was RIGHT and the route went right, but the ego's planned path bent left, away from the route, and it drove off the left edge of the road toward the shopping-center lot while slowing from 17 to 7 m/s. It ended up 12.8 m off the recorded human path, and after it left the road, actor 32 hit its rear.
